evidence.source: Education Ministry of Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: received Shuowen explanation and cited usages
evidence.text: The entry repeats the Shuowen explanation that 高 means 崇 and depicts a raised 臺觀. It gives early literary citations for not ascending high places in the Liji and for a high ridge in the Shijing, alongside examples for several later-listed senses. The entry’s list is not a chronology, and it does not establish that the earliest inscriptional use had the sense ‘high/tall’.
evidence.title: [A04667] 高 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: ShuoWen.org, received Shuowen entry and Duan Yucai annotation
evidence.text: The received entry glosses 高 as 崇, describes its form as a tall 臺觀, and analyzes it as 从冂、口, comparing it with 倉 and 舍. Duan Yucai’s annotation further explains the enclosure/building comparison. This records a traditional lexicographic account; it does not independently prove separate original semantic roles for 冂 and 口.
evidence.title: 說文解字「高」 - Shuowen.org

search_audit.outcome: Opened the official Taiwan dictionary and received Shuowen entry. Both supplied Unicode Unihan record URLs returned internal errors; local exact reading rows were available in the input packet and are reported as local metadata, not verified upstream-page contents.

gaps: No independently inspected glyph pixels were available: the Commons original-image links for the alternate files failed to open, and the proposed image sources therefore remain candidates rather than selected assets.
The exact Shuowen Seal Radical 187 Commons record and its imageinfo API lookup were inaccessible; its identity and reuse terms remain unverified.

The sources support a traditional tall raised-building interpretation, but do not verify a primary inscription context that securely establishes the earliest lexical sense or a dated semantic-development chain.
The traditional Shuowen segmentation into 冂 and 口 is documented, but their independent original semantic contributions are not established.

高 and 京 have distinct readings in the supplied local datasets (Unihan kMandarin 高 gāo / 京 jīng; Baxter–Sagart MC 高 kaw / 京 kjaeng and OC 高 *Cə.[k]ˤaw / 京 *[k]raŋ). No phonetic component or sound borrowing is proposed; resemblance and separate graph explanations do not establish common ancestry.
The official Unicode Unihan pages for U+9AD8 and U+4EAC could not be opened. The local reading rows are not represented as externally verified Unicode contents.

limitations.text: The exact Radical 187 file and imageinfo API lookup were inaccessible. Alternate Commons pages for 高-bigseal.svg and 高-bronze-shang.svg identify modern redrawings and report reuse metadata, but their original image links could not be opened, so no image is selected without pixel inspection.

The building/tower interpretation is supported by received Shuowen and dictionary descriptions, but the available text does not establish a specific dated graphic sequence or earliest lexical context.
